findings.issue: The protocol says the FRONTIER block's allowance is computed "from the node's remaining child slots". frontier-admit.cjs:612-615 takes the minimum of the node's remaining child slots and the run-wide remaining nodes (`maxFrontierNodes - countLiveNodes`), so in the shipped default flow the leaf's allowance is the run cap's remainder, not its child slots. With the six-seed default the derived budget is 16 (frontier-admit.cjs:269-276) and the cap 8, so a depth-1 node that has no children at all is told "You may append up to 2 `frontier_proposal` rows"; at an explicit 10-iteration budget the same node is told "This node has no child slots left". The doc leaves out the run-cap bound that actually sets the number the leaf sees.

fix.old: computes from the node's remaining child slots
fix.new: computes from the node's remaining child slots and the run's remaining nodes under the frontier cap

findings.issue: The FAN-OUT section blurb says the section "covers 4 scenarios" and then enumerates only three: "CLI lineage pool dispatch, native sequential agent dispatch, and single-executor parity". The fourth is DR-073 ("Fan-out deals seeded frontier nodes round-robin", line 909), the expansive frontier partition that fanout-run.cjs `partitionFrontierNodes`/`writeLineageFrontierStore` and the fanout-merge.cjs partition guard back. The enumeration the doc presents as the section's coverage leaves out the one fan-out behavior this topic adds.
